text.p: Mexican builder Bufete Industrial SA de CV mustered an impressive improvement in sales and operating margins during 1996 despite a weak construction industry, analysts said on Monday.
The company reported a loss of 0.88 peso per CPO share, much better than expectations of a loss of 1.45 pesos per share among five industry analysts surveyed by Reuters.

"The revenue growth is incredible, on a year over year basis as in a quarter over quarter comparison -- it's very good considering the weakness in the Mexican construction industry," said Ben Uglow, an analyst at Flemings Research in New York. Bufete's revenues were 4.397 billion pesos in 1996, up some 47 percent in real terms compared with 1995.

For the year, the company's operating margin rose to 4.8 percent compared with 2.5 percent the previous year. And during the fourth quarter alone, its margin rose to 6.1 percent compared with a negative 6.3 percent during the same period of 1995.

"The improvement in margins is noteworthy because they were able to cut costs in an environment where they were competing in public auctions for big projects," said Rafael Elias Linero, a construction analyst at CS First Boston in New York. "It's a big increase in margins, and one that I think is sustainable for 1996," agreed Flemings' Uglow.

Bufete's backlog of 3.263 billion pesos was not as big as some expectations, although analysts said it showed the company was the construction firm that best weathered the 1994-1995 peso crisis in Mexico, which caused a huge slump in the domestic economy.
Sobani Warner at Bear Stearns in New York sounded a note of caution for the year ahead by saying Bufete did face some pressure from rising local costs.

"With 50 percent of its backlog in dollars, margins could be squeezed by exposure to rising local costs" as well as any further real gains in the peso against the dollar, Warner said in a recent report.
